plan_a_advantages: More frequent easy runs could be beneficial for recovery and consistent volume.
The inclusion of strength sessions is a good addition for injury prevention and overall fitness.
plan_b_advantages: Directly addresses speed and power development with tempo and hill workouts.
Longer runs at a controlled pace are more effective for building trail-specific endurance than shorter, easy runs.
reasoning: Plan B is the better training plan for a trail runner aiming to become faster. It incorporates more structured, intensity-based workouts like tempo runs and hill sessions, which directly target improving speed and power – crucial for trail running. Plan A, while including some aerobic work, relies heavily on easy runs and strength sessions, which are important but don't provide the same level of stimulus for increasing running speed. Plan B’s inclusion of threshold work and hill repeats will build the specific adaptations needed for trail running efficiency and speed, whereas Plan A’s focus is more on building a base level of fitness.
